findings.title: Exact JSON numbers lose their identity during policy checks
findings.contract: The design requires enum/range enforcement and exact forwarding of large integers (tools/call; Decisions made while building).
findings.actual: An enum containing only 9007199254740992 accepts 9007199254740993. Minimum and maximum checks also collapse these values. Nested enum values have the same problem. Editing an unrelated description rounds an upstream schema const of 9007199254740993 down to 9007199254740992.
findings.fix: Keep JSON numbers exact in toolMap and schema materialization. Compare JSON numbers by mathematical value with a bounded exact decimal/integer representation, recursively for enums. Preserve equality of 1, 1.0 and 1e0; do not compare only their bytes or coerce strings into numbers. Preserve values during forwarding. For values CEL cannot represent, return a defined evaluation error when a rule needs that value instead of silently rounding it.

findings.title: Call rules do not see all effective arguments
findings.contract: Call rules judge effective arguments before execution; pins force values and defaults fill missing arguments.
findings.actual: When the client omits a visible pinned tenant, the tenant is absent during policy evaluation and appears only before forwarding. A deny conditioned on that tenant is bypassed. Defaults on added parameters disappear because defaults are recorded only for nonempty upstream identities.
findings.fix: Build one effective exposed argument map containing defaults and visible pins before evaluating call rules. Keep added-parameter defaults under their own identities. Preserve the existing rejection of conflicting client pin values, and reassert pins after patches before final validation and reversal.

findings.title: Hiding an added parameter permits it to reach the upstream
findings.contract: Hidden parameters reject client values. Added parameters are removed before forwarding.
findings.actual: Adding internal and then hiding it removes it from both Added and Hidden. Supplying internal:"injected" is treated as an unknown extra property and forwarded.
findings.fix: Track parameter origin, visibility and current name independently. Keep tombstones for hidden added parameters, reject their client keys, and strip every added identity during reversal even after rename or hide.

findings.title: Reply hooks inspect different arguments from those sent upstream
findings.contract: tools/input and tools/result receive args as sent upstream. Prompt input has the corresponding request context.
findings.actual: A call patch changes n from 1 to 2, and forwarding sends 2, but result/input rules read 1. prompts/input receives an empty argument map, even after argument renames and patches.
findings.fix: Return an immutable call execution context alongside Forward, containing the exact upstream args, original item identity, exposed view and policy snapshot. Pass that context into reply handlers. Do not recompute arguments from the client request or rerun non-idempotent patches.

findings.title: A resource hidden by the listing pipeline can still be read
findings.contract: Hidden items must be unreadable; evaluation errors fail closed; applicable denies are final.
findings.actual: Resources and templates hidden by a modify evaluation error remain readable. Duplicate resource identities are hidden by listItems collision handling, but readCheck still selects the raw catalog resource and forwards the read.
findings.fix: Use one resolved visibility result for list, direct read, directory filtering and fallback. It must include filter decisions, modify failures and identity collisions. Preserve legitimate template-only resources by applying the same template visibility checks without requiring a concrete resource listing.

findings.title: Template matching authorizes URIs outside the template
findings.contract: A URI must be covered by a listing or a matching RFC 6570 template. slugUris rewrites only URIs owned by that upstream.
findings.actual: file:///teams/{team}/public/{file} authorizes file:///teams/blue/private/key. A simple {file} accepts raw slash-separated descendants. slugUris ignores template suffixes and rewrites a /private URI for a template ending in /public.
findings.fix: Use a tested RFC 6570-aware matcher that respects every literal segment and operator, including the distinction between {x} and {+x}. Where inversion is unsupported, do not infer ownership from a prefix. Reuse the same ownership predicate in fallback, read authorization and slugUris.

findings.title: Directory MIME type bypasses resource and template filters
findings.contract: Directory reads apply the same visibility check to each child and drop hidden children.
findings.actual: Children marked inode/directory receive only the denied-skill-folder check. A directory denied by resources/filter or templates/filter is still returned.
findings.fix: Run resource filters, applicable template filters and skill ancestor denies for every child regardless of MIME type. Separate directory existence/containment checks from visibility so valid directory-only entries are still supported.

findings.title: Binary resource data bypasses a result deny
findings.contract: resources/result can deny a read result. The MCP resource content model supports both text and blob values.
findings.actual: A rule with when:true and decision:"deny" is never evaluated for a blob content item. The reply returns the binary data successfully.
findings.fix: Run result decision rules for every content item, including blobs. Permit text mutation only when text is present, preserving blob bytes and MIME type otherwise. An unconditional deny must block the whole result for either representation.

findings.title: Read responses retain public cache scope after caller-specific policy
findings.contract: Every gateway CacheableResult must carry gateway ttlMs and cacheScope:"private". The protocol permits public results to be shared across authorization contexts.
findings.actual: Resource and directory read replies retain the upstream cacheScope:"public" and ttlMs:99999 despite gateway ttlMs:123. Results can depend on caller-specific filters or shaping.
findings.fix: Finalize all CacheableResult variants through one response helper that sets private scope and the configured gateway TTL. Apply it after shaping and before size checks. Do not add cache fields to result types that are not CacheableResult.

findings.title: Listing and input-required outputs bypass size limits
findings.contract: The design caps listings/results and checks size again after shaping.
findings.actual: Oversized tool, resource and skill listings succeed. A tiny tool list expanded by a modify rule also succeeds. Input message shaping can produce a response larger than MaxResponseBytes without rejection.
findings.fix: Apply a final serialized-output cap to every response branch, including input_required and listings, after mux prefixes and state wrapping. Bound intermediate rule output too. The transport adapter must separately enforce upstream raw/decompressed limits before allocation; catalog-only scenarios cannot prove that transport boundary.

findings.title: Custom helpers are effectively unmetered
findings.contract: Every helper must have a cost estimate feeding the CEL cost limit.
findings.actual: drop over one row and over 10,000 rows both report an actual CEL cost of 3. The helper performs recursive copying outside meaningful cost accounting.
findings.fix: Register runtime overload cost estimators based on visited input nodes and paths, plus compile-time estimates where supported. Bound traversal, depth and allocation before performing the work. Add interrupt checks within long helper traversals so a single helper cannot monopolize the request budget.

findings.title: Expired rule contexts can still return success or forward
findings.contract: Exceeding the request rule budget is an evaluation error that denies.
findings.actual: With an already expired rule context, prompts/get and resources/read forward, and prompt/resource listings succeed after simple rules. CEL interruption checks during comprehensions do not enforce every deadline.
findings.fix: Check the shared rule deadline before and after each evaluation and at every final success/forward boundary. Propagate the same budget across the operation. Distinguish this enforcement deadline from the separate bounded audit budget described in F13.

findings.title: Audit work can change an allowed call into a denial
findings.contract: Audit matches and failures must not change outcomes. The design also imposes a request budget; its precedence needs an explicit rule.
findings.actual: The baseline forwards. Adding only an audit rule that exceeds the five-millisecond rule budget produces an isError refusal. This reproduces three consecutive times.
findings.fix: Give audit evaluation a separate bounded budget and record its exhaustion as an audit error, without consuming the enforcement deadline. Specify how incomplete audit traces are represented after exhaustion; an unconditional complete-log promise cannot coexist with finite limits.

findings.title: Skill read bytes contradict rewrite rejection and advertised digests
findings.contract: Request-dependent skill rewrites are skipped. A name-changing rewrite is rejected atomically for the whole skill, preserving upstream bytes.
findings.actual: skills/get keeps original digests for clock/caller-dependent rules, while resources/read applies those rules. After a rejected name rewrite, reading SKILL.md still returns the changed name. A supporting file is also rewritten despite the skill-wide rollback.
findings.fix: Centralize the skill rewrite plan and use it for manifest construction and file reads. A skipped or rejected plan must serve original bytes for every file. Validate all files and root frontmatter before accepting a plan; recompute from live content per request, consistent with the no-content-cache design.

findings.title: Malformed rule documents can silently discard the denying policy
findings.contract: The rules wrapper is JSON and invalid rule lists fail closed. Arguments must be one JSON object.
findings.actual: Parse accepts [] followed by a second denying rule array, or by garbage, and returns an empty policy. decodeArgs accepts multiple JSON documents such as {} {} and uses only the first. Fuzz seed checks reproduce both.
findings.fix: After decoding the expected root value, require EOF after whitespace. Preserve all valid whitespace and member-order variations. Keep the intentionally supported multi-document scenario/JSONL loader separate. Retain the design-required duplicate-key and depth checks; do not reject ordinary additional argument properties solely to fix this parser issue.

findings.title: Fallback reports candidates that effective authorization rejects
findings.contract: Fallback candidates are limited to visible matches after filters, with no guessing.
findings.actual: A resource covered by a denied template still becomes an exact candidate. A template-only URI denied by resources/filter still becomes a template candidate. Both create false ambiguity with the one readable server.
findings.fix: Authorize each candidate using the complete resource-read visibility predicate before reduction. Preserve exact-match precedence and refusal when an eligible catalog is unavailable. Use the same predicate to avoid disclosing denied manifest-only candidates.

findings.title: Canonical URI refusal is not applied to returned identities
findings.contract: The design refuses dot segments, empty segments and percent-encoded unreserved characters to keep resource identity consistent.
findings.actual: A directory response returns file:///public/%61, although directly reading that URI is refused. Substituted read content under file:///public/%62 also passes authorization.
findings.fix: Validate every returned resource identity before containment or policy checks. Apply the same documented canonical rules as on inbound reads; drop invalid directory children and refuse or drop invalid substituted content consistently. Do not blanket-reject reserved percent escapes; see A01.

findings.title: Changing one parameter turns an unrelated false schema into an accepting schema
findings.contract: The overlay changes only targeted properties. MCP allows JSON Schema keywords and boolean property schemas.
findings.actual: Changing q.description changes an untouched forbidden:false property into forbidden:{}, reversing that property schema’s meaning.
findings.fix: Preserve boolean property schemas as booleans when unchanged. If a rule annotates a boolean schema, wrap it in a semantically equivalent schema such as allOf:[false] plus the annotation. Never coerce false to an empty accepting schema or reject a valid untouched schema.

findings.title: Empty skill files are omitted from digest recomputation
findings.contract: Rewriting a skill file recomputes digest and byte size for the bytes later returned.
findings.actual: An empty text file rewritten to "filled" retains the empty-file digest and size zero in skills/get; resources/read returns "filled".
findings.fix: Represent text presence separately from its value, for example with a pointer or explicit content kind. Run rewrite rules on present empty text and update its digest and byte size. Keep binary and absent files distinguishable.

findings.title: Nested SKILL.md files are mistaken for the enclosing skill identity
findings.contract: The Skills spec treats nested skill files as supporting content of the enclosing skill. Each skill has its own identity.
findings.actual: Rewriting descriptions in a parent and child SKILL.md rejects the parent plan because the unchanged child name differs from the parent name.
findings.fix: Mirror frontmatter and enforce the parent name only for the entry’s exact root SKILL.md URI. Validate nested files against their own skill identity where applicable, while hashing them as supporting files of the parent.

findings.title: Dynamic skill frontmatter is not mirrored after a static rewrite
findings.contract: Dynamic skills omit digests, but hosts still compare returned SKILL.md frontmatter with the entry.
findings.actual: A resources:"dynamic" skill keeps description:"original" in skills/get while the same static rule returns description:"updated" on read.
findings.fix: Validate and mirror root frontmatter for dynamic skills as well as manifest-backed skills, keeping resources:"dynamic". If deterministic frontmatter cannot be produced, skip the rewrite consistently for entry and read rather than publish conflicting values.

findings.title: Rewrite frontmatter parsing accepts invalid skill metadata
findings.contract: Skills require name and description. Rewritten entry frontmatter must equal the served SKILL.md frontmatter.
findings.actual: The engine accepts a rewritten skill without description and a closing delimiter spelled ---not-a-fence. The upstream test server uses a separate, stricter parser, contrary to the catalogue’s single-parser claim.
findings.fix: Share one frontmatter parser and validator between fixture manifest generation and engine rewriting. Require a complete delimiter line and required typed fields. Preserve supported BOM/CRLF forms and arbitrary valid author metadata; do not curate metadata to a fixed subset. Reject invalid rewrite plans atomically.

findings.title: Search definitions merge distinct case-sensitive identities
findings.contract: Names reverse exactly; the protocol says tool names should be treated as case-sensitive.
findings.actual: Read and read remain distinct callable tools, but get_tool_definition lowercases both keys and returns read’s description for Read.
findings.fix: Index and resolve definitions by the exact exposed name, matching CallTool. Case-insensitive search ranking may remain a convenience, but exact definition lookup and dispatch must retain the selected identity.

findings.title: Direct-route search returns names that direct execution cannot resolve
findings.contract: Search mode is available on direct and mux routes and uses the same execution pipeline.
findings.actual: ToolSearch on a direct route returns a__lookup, but ExecuteTool on that route searches for the literal upstream name a__lookup and returns unknown tool.
findings.fix: Represent route topology and search mode separately. Prefix exposed names only on mux routes, and share one exposed-name formatter/resolver across search, definition lookup, listing and execution.

findings.title: dropSchema does not mirror wildcard deletion
findings.contract: dropSchema removes the schema properties that drop removes from values, including required entries.
findings.actual: dropSchema(schema,["*"]) leaves root properties a and b and required:[a,b] intact, while drop(value,["*"]) removes all fields.
findings.fix: Implement terminal wildcard deletion for object properties and matching requirements; preserve the appropriate empty-array semantics for array wildcards. Add paired data/schema tests. For reference-based schemas, support the requested transformation or return an explicit unsupported-edit error rather than silently leaving the schema unchanged.

findings.title: Tool result rules cannot access the documented meta alias
findings.contract: tools/result exposes result.meta for upstream result metadata.
findings.actual: The wire uses _meta, but resultVar never creates meta. Reading result.meta.trace therefore denies a valid upstream result with an evaluation error.
findings.fix: Expose a read-only result.meta alias of the original _meta map, with an empty map when absent. Keep _meta on the wire and preserve the existing metadata allowlist policy at its specified boundary.

findings.title: Discovery does not describe the implemented 2026 protocol surface
findings.contract: DiscoverResult requires supportedVersions. Clients call skills methods only after observing the Skills extension declaration.
findings.actual: Discover omits supportedVersions and never declares the Skills extension while skills/list succeeds. It also places server identity at the legacy top level rather than the spec’s optional _meta key.
findings.fix: Emit supportedVersions:["2026-07-28"] and derive extension capabilities from the methods actually exposed on the route. Declare directoryRead only where supported. Put display identity under _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"] when enabled; that identity field is SHOULD/optional, whereas supportedVersions is required.

findings.title: The engine does not implement property-level copy-on-write
findings.contract: The item view points at the cached upstream object; changing one property preserves untouched sibling pointers and avoids whole-schema copying.
findings.actual: The engine marshals and unmarshals the whole tool before evaluation, then again for changed output. Updating q.description loses pointer identity for an untouched tenant schema. Isolated View tests do not exercise this path.
findings.fix: Build views over cached decoded objects or a lazy typed adapter, and apply path overlays directly. Materialize only changed paths at response time. Retain the existing concurrency guarantees and test pointer identity through the actual ListTools pipeline.

findings.title: An audit-only patch satisfies hidden-required validation without supplying a value
findings.contract: Hiding a required parameter needs a supplying pin/default or an effective call patch. Audit rules never change arguments.
findings.actual: callFilled includes audit rules. A required tenant hidden without a default or pin is forwarded absent because an audit-only rule syntactically names args.tenant.
findings.fix: Exclude audit rules from static supplying-rule analysis. More generally, verify after actual call evaluation that each hidden required upstream parameter has a supplied value; merely finding a conditional assignment in the policy is insufficient.

findings.title: The scenario runner drops search continuation fields
findings.contract: execute_tool uses the complete tools/call pipeline, including continuation parameters.
findings.actual: The runner decodes only name and arguments, discarding requestState and inputResponses. The equivalent direct Engine.ExecuteTool API test passes.
findings.fix: Decode continuation fields in the scenario step and invoke Engine.ExecuteTool with them. Keep CX-53 as a runner regression test. This is a harness defect, not evidence that Engine.ExecuteTool drops state.

findings.title: Scenario equality assertions can certify the wrong large integer
findings.contract: Tests claiming exact numeric preservation must distinguish mathematically different JSON numbers.
findings.actual: An expectation equals:9007199254740992 passes against an observed json.Number("9007199254740993") because both sides are normalized through float64.
findings.fix: Decode expected values with UseNumber and compare recursively using an exact semantic comparator independent of the engine’s policy comparator. Accept equivalent number spellings, preserve array order, ignore object key order, and keep JSON strings/booleans distinct from numbers.

findings.title: Current profiling instrumentation panics when the rule set is nil
findings.contract: No matching rules allows by default. Existing Set methods explicitly handle a nil rules receiver.
findings.actual: An Engine.ListTools request with a valid catalog and Server.Rules:nil panics at s.prof. These profiling accesses appeared in external edits during this review.
findings.fix: Resolve the optional profile pointer through a nil-safe accessor, or normalize absent rules at the public engine boundary. Preserve nil/default behavior consistently across listing and call APIs. Keep profiling disabled by default.

findings.title: Valid upstream input requests lose answers when requestState is omitted
findings.contract: InputRequiredResult may contain inputRequests without requestState. The state field is optional in MCP 2026-07-28.
findings.actual: For tools, prompts and resources, the gateway wraps a valid challenge but forwards inputResponses only if the upstream state string is nonempty. Stateless upstream prompts therefore lose the answers.
findings.fix: Track a validated upstream continuation independently of the optional upstream state value. Forward its validated responses even when requestState is absent; preserve any supplied opaque state exactly. This protocol fix is independent of the planned KV storage.

findings.title: Valid state-only input-required replies bypass wrapping
findings.contract: MCP explicitly permits input_required containing requestState without inputRequests, for example load shedding.
findings.actual: Prompt and resource reply handlers recognize input_required only when inputRequests is a map. A state-only reply returns the raw upstream token, which the next request rejects as invalid gateway state.
findings.fix: Dispatch by resultType first. Handle both permitted forms: requests with optional state, and state-only. Wrap any upstream state for routing/binding without requiring an elicitation capability when no user input is requested. Do not fabricate input requests.

findings.title: Resource, template and skill order differs from the agreed name order
findings.contract: The design decisions require slug a-z followed by name a-z.
findings.actual: Resources and templates sort by URI identity; skills sort by URI ancestry. A name alpha with URI z sorts after zebra with URI a.
findings.fix: Sort each slug’s final visible records by exposed name, with URI as a stable tiebreaker. If URI order is preferred for some kinds, revise the design and catalogue explicitly rather than claiming the current global name-order contract is proven.

findings.title: Equivalent integral JSON spellings produce different policy outcomes
findings.contract: The input schema declares an integer. JSON Schema integer semantics accept numeric values with zero fractional part, independently of decimal or exponent spelling. The adapter itself promises int64 when integral.
findings.actual: With a call rule args.n + 1, the input 1 forwards n:2. The valid equivalent spellings 1.0, 1e0, 1E+0 and 0.1e1 all produce an isError result with a CEL no-such-overload error. Int64 parses the token spelling, and the fallback turns the equivalent values into doubles.
findings.fix: Normalize numeric values for CEL from exact mathematical value and the declared schema, rather than lexical spelling. An in-range integral value under an integer schema must have the same CEL type for all valid JSON representations. Keep raw argument values separate for forwarding. Preserve fractional numbers where permitted and do not coerce quoted numbers or booleans.
